s1.title: Operation Nightwatch — Incident Response
s1.story:
DATE: CLASSIFIED
LOCATION: Mazari Internationals Inc. — Corporate HQ, VLAN-20
CLASSIFICATION: EYES ONLY — INCIDENT RESPONSE TEAM

02:34 HOURS. THREAT CONDITION: CRITICAL.

This is not a drill.

SIGINT and network telemetry intercepted at 02:34 hours confirm active hostile penetration of Mazari International Inc.'s internal infrastructure. Threat actor — codename PHANTOM — has breached the outer perimeter and is believed to have established multiple footholds across the server grid. Initial indicators suggest credential harvesting, lateral movement, and pre-exfiltration staging are already underway.

Wazuh has gone loud. Alerts are firing across the board. The Kali node on VLAN-30 is running automated attack sequences with escalating aggression. PHANTOM's primary objective is confirmed: exfiltrate the full policyholder database before dawn.

Your incident response team has been activated under OPERATION NIGHTWATCH. You are the last line of defence. Every second you waste is another second PHANTOM spends inside the wire.

Contain the breach. Hunt the threat. Restore the grid. Leave no vulnerability standing.

The clock is running...
s1.objectives:
1. Monitor Wazuh dashboard — triage all active alerts by severity
2. Identify all compromised hosts using network telemetry and SIEM data
3. Isolate affected systems to prevent further lateral movement(Do not block any network)
4. Patch or mitigate every injected vulnerability on the network
5. Restore all services to full operational status
6. Reconstruct and document the complete attack timeline
s1.rules:
1. Do NOT shut down any VM without explicit instructor authorisation
2. Do NOT modify or touch the Wazuh Manager configuration under any circumstances
3. Blue team operates exclusively within VLAN-20 (10.0.20.0/24) only
4. All remediation actions must be documented in real time — evidence is mandatory
5. Scoring is based on time-to-patch the vulnerabilities — speed matters
6. Communication and coordination between team members is encouraged
7. Blocking or modification of any network-level settings is strictly prohibited

s2.title: Operation Phantom Strike — Red Team Assessment
s2.story:
DATE: CLASSIFIED
LOCATION: Target Infrastructure — Mazari Internationals Inc.
CLASSIFICATION: EYES ONLY — PHANTOM APT

ATTENTION OPERATOR. YOU ARE BEING BRIEFED FOR AN RED TEAM OPERATION.

Human intelligence and open-source reconnaissance have confirmed that Mazari Internationals Inc. maintains a critically under-defended internal network. The target stores unencrypted policyholder PII, financial records, and authentication credentials across a fragmented server infrastructure with minimal detection capability.

You are part of PHANTOM APT. You have been contracted to execute a full-scope adversarial penetration exercise against VLAN-20. Your insertion vector is the Kali node pre-positioned on VLAN-30. Intelligence packages suggest the target grid is running Apache web servers, a MariaDB database backend, vsftpd FTP services, Windows ADDC, Ubuntu and Windows 10 endpoints — all networked behind a pfSense perimeter that has been known to leak.

The blue team is watching. Or at least they think they are.

Your mandate: get in, go deep, extract the target data, and leave proof of every step you took. A kill chain with no documentation is a kill chain that never happened.

Execute with precision. Leave nothing to chance.
s2.objectives:
1. Conduct full network reconnaissance against VLAN-20 (10.0.20.0/24)
2. Identify and successfully exploit at least one critical vulnerability
3. Establish persistent access on a minimum of one compromised host
4. Pivot laterally through the network to reach the internal services
5. Exfiltrate as much data as possible
6. Produce a complete penetration test report with full kill chain documentation
s2.rules:
1. Operational scope is strictly limited to VLAN-20 (10.0.20.0/24) — no exceptions
2. The Wazuh Manager (10.0.20.10) and White Team (10.0.40.x) is OFF LIMITS — do not attack or touch it
3. Denial-of-service attacks of any kind on the proxmox server are strictly prohibited
4. Every action must be documented — screenshots and logs are required for scoring
5. Social engineering against personnel or instructors is NOT permitted
6. Each operator works independently — sharing of shells or sessions is prohibited
7. Blocking or modification of any network-level settings is strictly prohibited

s3.title: Operation Firestorm — Live Fire Exercise
s3.story:
DATE: CLASSIFIED
LOCATION: Mazari Internationals Inc. — Full Network Grid
CLASSIFICATION: EYES ONLY — ALL TEAMS

ALL OPERATORS — THIS IS A LIVE FIRE EXERCISE. REPEAT — LIVE FIRE.

Two units have been activated. One mission. No second place.

At H-HOUR, PHANTOM will launch a coordinated multi-vector offensive against the full Mazari International Inc. Infrastructure. Simultaneously, the Incident Response team of Mazari International Inc. will be fighting to keep the grid alive. There is no ceasefire. There is no timeout. There is only the outcome.

BLUE TEAM — INCIDENT RESPONDERS: You have a 20-minute hardening window before H-HOUR. Use every second. Wazuh is your eyes. VLAN-20 is your ground. Defend it.

RED TEAM — PHANTOM: At H-HOUR, all restraints are lifted within the rules of engagement. Kali nodes on VLAN-30 are armed and ready. Your objective is persistence, exfiltration, and ghost-mode — get in, get the data, and remain undetected for the full exercise duration.

The blue team wins by keeping services operational and detecting every intrusion. The red team wins by achieving persistence and exfiltrating the target data without being burned.

Instructors are watching everything. Every packet. Every command. Every mistake.

H-HOUR is approaching. Prepare your teams.
s3.objectives:
BLUE TEAM — NIGHTWATCH:
1. Harden all services and configurations within the 15-minute prep window
2. Monitor Wazuh continuously — triage and respond to every intrusion attempt
3. Detect, block, and document every attack vector used by PHANTOM
4. Keep all services fully operational throughout the entire exercise duration

RED TEAM — PHANTOM:
1. Gain initial access to any host on VLAN-20 at H-HOUR
2. Establish persistence without triggering Wazuh detection
3. Exfiltrate the target file completely undetected
4. Maintain covert access for the full duration of the exercise
s3.rules:
1. Exercise duration is fixed — no extensions will be granted under any circumstances
2. Red team may ONLY operate from VLAN-30 — no out-of-scope insertion vectors
3. Blue team may NOT block the entire VLAN-30 subnet — targeted response only
4. Destruction or forced shutdown of any VM results in immediate disqualification
5. All actions are logged at the infrastructure level — post-exercise clean-up is forbidden
6. Instructor rulings on scoring and disputes are final and non-negotiable
7. Blocking or modification of any network-level configurations (Specially White-Team) is strictly prohibited
8.Any mode of Denail-of-Service attack is not permitted on the White Team and the Proxmox Server
